significance: A 9th-century Chola foundation near Chennai, extended by later Cholas, Pandyas and the Vijayanagara rulers, with an unusual Gaja Prishtam (elephant-back) vimana. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam revered in the 7th-century Tevaram and belongs to the Shakti triad of Tondaimandalam.
story: The temple's tradition tells of King Thondaiman striking a lingam hidden in dense mullai thickets during a campaign; Shiva and Parvati appeared, helped him defeat two brothers, and he raised the temple on the spot.
